newsitem.title: UK: British mad cow costs to top 4.0 bln pounds -paper.
newsitem.headline: British mad cow costs to top 4.0 bln pounds -paper.

text.p: Chancellor Gordon Brown has been warned by Treasury officials the cost of Britain's BSE crisis will top 4.0 billion pounds ($6.7 billion), the Times reported in its Friday edition.
The paper said the cost of the "mad cow disease" crisis will overshoot the 2.0 billion estimate made by the previous government by 700 million pounds this year.
It said the increased costs were the result of a serious underestimation of the number of cows slaughtered, the cost of their destruction and storage for carcasses awaiting incineration.
The crisis is now costing Britain a million pounds a day and the overall cost is estimated by the Treasury to be 4.2 billion pounds, the paper said.
Earlier on Thursday hamburger chain McDonald's Corp gave Britain's beleaguered farming industry a boost by saying it would resume buying British beef for sale in its 764 restaurants in the country.
The move was the most significant victory for the industry since the onset of the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) crisis 15 months ago.

It was hailed by Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham as sending a message to other European Union states who have prohibited exports of British beef since March 1996 that they should review the ban speedily.

The EU ban followed new scientific evidence suggesting it was possible for people eating beef from cows suffering from BSE to contract the human version of the brain-wasting disorder, Creutzfeldt-Jacob disease.

The Times said the disclosure of unforseen spending commitments facing the Labour government would "inevitably be seen as preparing the ground for higher than expected tax increases" in its first budget, due to be presented by Brown next Wednesday. REUTER AS ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
